scope: Unified 3D R&D evidence-first material delta since 2026-10-09 morning local time

findings.materiality: Promotes collection import, reload, and localize behavior to explicit reproducibility controls in EXP-BLENDER-ASSET-AS-CODE-001; does not promote Blender 5.3 to production.
findings.source_quality: A: merged upstream implementation, removal of the experimental option, and upstream Python import regression tests. June meeting provides prior blocker history, not evidence that all edge cases are solved.
verified_evidence: On Oct 9 Blender implemented Collection Import clear/reload/make_local operators; the reload is specified as clear followed by import.
On Oct 9 upstream removed the experimental use_collection_importer gate and Blender-v5.3 release branch no longer contains it.
Earlier on Oct 6 multi-archive-library import landed. This corroborates richer external source handling but not universal dependency fidelity.
limitation_or_disagreement: Commit on development/release branch does not mean Blender 5.3 stable is shipped.
Clear+reload can change object IDs, reset imported state, or break local overrides; those are test hypotheses, not verified defects.
Collection import is not the same as text-based node graph source authority; it may solve reproducible asset ingestion without solving source diff/merge.
findings.engineering_design_implication: Expand the asset-as-code experiment into two source-authority axes: diffable procedural definitions and idempotent linked collection ingestion. In a clean Blender 5.3 test environment, import a packaged Gaudi element and a product asset, capture stable semantic object IDs, mesh/material hashes, licensing/provenance and relative dependencies; edit upstream source; reload; validate identity retention, materials, hierarchy, local edits, path portability and reproducibility. Test make_local then verify the result is decoupled. Keep production .blend authority unchanged.

new_acceptance: Relative source paths survive moving fixture to a second checkout.
Reload after a source revision causes no stale duplicate collections and preserves/explicitly remaps semantic IDs.
Mesh geometry/material hashes are deterministic for unchanged source; documented diffs match expected revisions.
Source-level provenance and asset licenses stay attached after reload and make_local.
Failure leaves a recoverable original and does not mutate production libraries.

findings.materiality: Changes ClusterLOD and generated-product geometry-quality validation to include normals/corner continuity and hard-edge correctness on degenerates, instead of assuming topology/triangle-count checks are sufficient.
findings.source_quality: A: upstream merged code and explicit degenerate-normal regression test. No external performance or visual benchmark.
verified_evidence: meshoptimizer changed corner grouping so degenerate triangles adjacent to a valid triangle inherit normals from the adjacent faces.
The implementation explicitly avoids treating degenerate triangles as bridges for smoothing across separate nondegenerate surfaces.
Upstream notes fully degenerate groups and extremely narrow nonzero-area slivers may still produce zero normals; large-index guards were also added.
limitation_or_disagreement: This affects normal generation and vertex reindexing quality, not a demonstrated FPS or file-size improvement.
Behavior on Gaudi, helmet shells, shoes, bikes and procedural room architecture remains unmeasured.
Hard-edge conservation must be measured because normal inheritance can be visually helpful yet inappropriate across intended creases.
findings.engineering_design_implication: Amend procedural mesh hygiene QA and EXP-CLUSTERLOD-001 to use authored stress meshes plus representative assets containing zero-area/collinear/near-degenerate triangles; compare released v1.3 and pinned post-v1.3 commit for zero/NaN normals, normal discontinuity, hard-edge leakage, reindexed vertex count, geometric fidelity and glTF round-trip appearance. Preserve source geometry and stable release baseline.

new_acceptance: Hard edges remain hard across degenerate bridge triangles.
Quantify zero and non-finite normals; flag rather than silently repair unrecoverable all-degenerate groups.
Compare vertex growth after reindexing and rendered normal-buffer diffs, separately from HLOD timings.
Do not conflate normal-generation improvements with real-time rendering performance.

watch_only.reason: Merged MaterialXLoader nodedef default correctness fix could improve look-development interchange, but direct MaterialX dependency/usage in the active products is not established; record as compatibility regression candidate, not a new priority.
Specification wording corrected absolute GLB file-size limit; no evidence of assets approaching multi-GiB single-GLB boundaries; retain small composable assets.
Correctness fixes are relevant to dev-renderer regression checks but do not alter the existing isolated r187 experiment or shipped version selection.
Catalan UPC listing for Oct 10 Palau Guell engineering event is an event announcement, not measured new engineering scholarship or primary historical evidence.

no_new_decision_changing_findings: Catalan/Spanish Gaudi historical evidence beyond the previously adopted force-vs-documented-geometry distinction
glTF 2.1 composable external references and world packaging
Product visualization claims specific to watches/bikes/shoes/helmets
3DGS/NeRF/splat hybrid interoperability beyond the pre-existing experiments
Sports physics, generic cycling aero/CFD, rolling resistance, wind and terrain
program_decision: No architecture or ranked experiment priority change. Amend two existing experiments and keep production untouched; upstream changes alone are not proof of benchmark benefits.
